comment: Personal blog, mostly on small cloud tiers, with DuckDB on a 16 GB laptop. Ranked by total time; by geometric mean Power BI Datamart comes first. The author says single slow queries skew SingleStore and DuckDB.
evidence: Re-read November 2026. datamonkeysite.com, TPC-H SF10, total seconds over 22 queries from results.csv (May 2022) in github.com/djouallah/Testing_BI_Engine: Snowflake X-Small 23.1, Power BI Datamart 31.2 (specification undisclosed), SingleStore S-0 33.2, BigQuery on demand with 1 GB BI Engine 35.0, Databricks 2X-Small 58.4, DuckDB on a laptop 71.4. Q13 skews SingleStore and Q9 skews DuckDB, per the author.

comment: Run by Data-Sleek, a SingleStore consultancy, on 11 of the 22 queries. Four queries needed extra memory on ClickHouse, which could not complete Q11. ClickHouse loaded the largest tables about twice as fast.
evidence: Re-read November 2026. Text table "SingleStore vs. ClickHouse Queries", Q1-Q11, one 64 GB / 8 CPU machine, scale factor not stated. SingleStore is faster on 9 of 11 (ClickHouse leads on Q1, 0 vs 20 ms, and Q7, 16.4 vs 18.1 s). Q8-Q11 failed on ClickHouse until memory was raised.

comment: Published by Rockset about its own product, and now offline. Its ClickHouse total (1,112 ms) matches one Altinity published in 2021 on different hardware, so this may not be a like-for-like run.
evidence: The source URL redirects to OpenAI's announcement that it acquired Rockset, so the post itself could not be re-read. Search excerpts of it (November 2026) give Rockset 664 ms, Druid 747 ms and ClickHouse 1,112 ms over 13 queries. Altinity's March 2021 post reports ClickHouse at 1.112 s on one m5.8xlarge.

comment: Published by Onehouse, which sells Hudi-based products. Corrected November 2026 to a tie: the post calls the released versions (Hudi 0.11.1, Delta Lake 1.2.0) practically equal. Only Hudi's unreleased code was about 5% faster.
evidence: Re-read November 2026. Text only; both charts are images. Queries: no practical difference between Hudi 0.11.1 and Delta 1.2.0, Hudi master about 5% faster. Loading within 5-6% of each other. AWS EMR 6.6.0, Spark 3.2.0; cluster size and scale factor not stated. Hudi was run with bulk_insert and its metadata table and meta-fields disabled. Recorded as a Hudi win until November 2026; the tie compares released versions.

comment: Analyst article favourable to Oracle that doesn't say who ran the test. Transaction speed was equal, so the analytics half decides. One of its throughput sentences appears to swap the two figures.
evidence: Analyst article on Oracle's MySQL HeatWave launch, vendor-favourable; it does not name who ran the test. CH-benCHmark 100G: OLTP equal (0.02 s latency, 30K transactions/min for both), so the OLAP side decides: 4 concurrent OLAP sessions, HeatWave 35 s vs Aurora db.r5.8xlarge 632 s latency (18x). The OLAP throughput sentence claims 110x for HeatWave but prints .06 for HeatWave and 6.6 for Aurora, apparently swapped.

comment: HEAVY.AI timed out on 37 of 113 queries. Each counts as the 120 s limit, so its real time would be longer.
evidence: UC Merced technical report, section 5.6 and Table 6, total time for the 113 JOB queries with each engine's default optimizer, no indexes, same CPU server: DuckDB 30.38s, MonetDB 114.46s, HEAVY.AI 4744s (37 queries hit the 120s timeout, each charged as 120s, so a lower bound). Forced-join-order (no-CE) runs not counted; PostgreSQL left out because the paper runs it tuned, with a different timeout, and does not tabulate it against these three.

comment: DuckDB ran embedded and the others in Docker. PostgreSQL had 23 extra indexes. The report has no publication date; we use the commit that added it.

DuckDB runs embedded, the others in Docker. Date is the commit that added the report.

evidence: BenchBox Results table, TPC-H SF 1, power phase, 22 queries, untuned standard runs (Apple M4 for local engines), geomean query time: DuckDB 35 and 38 ms, Polars 36 and 37 ms (repeat runs interleave, so a tie), DataFusion 47 ms, ClickHouse Local 70 ms, SQLite 494 ms, Spark SQL 719 ms, Snowflake X-Small 943 ms, Databricks 2X-Small 956 ms, BigQuery 1.04 s.
